b: Democrats finally turned Texas blue, winning not just the Senate seat but every statewide office in the process as well as a majority in the state legislature. This wasn’t a fluke win for Democrats; Republicans can expect elections in Texas to be competitive for the rest of this decade.

This has big impacts for presidential elections going forward. Democrats just opened a new path to the presidency: win Texas, and just ONE other swing state from the rust belt (MI PA WI) or the sun belt (AZ GA NC NV) while holding their safe states.

This means pretty much the entire election will be decided by who wins Texas. Assuming current trends hold, you’re gonna get to a situation where one singular state will decide the presidency. Candidates from both parties will spend 80 percent of their time, money, and resources in just Texas alone.

At that point, the electoral college will become a truly ridiculous exercise. The GOP knows they have no chance at winning the presidency if Texas goes blue, and Democrats have no real incentive to keep the electoral college given that it has historically disadvantaged their candidates (Gore in 2000, Clinton in 2016). The other 49 states in this country won’t take kindly to being sidelined every election cycle going forward and the chance of getting a constitutional amendment to abandon the electoral college will finally have a chance at passage.
